Subject: Commit gating & CS readiness sync - Horizon Health (HZN-4382)

Hi Sophie —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Finance is doing a mid-quarter review and asked us to confirm the commit picture for Q4 so they can finalize the expansion forecast. I wanted to align with you and Monica (CS) on a couple of items before we lock things in: 

- Confirm expected signed date window (we have been tracking Oct 15–31).
- Final ARR uplift and billing cadence (annual vs. monthly).
- Any outstanding security/compliance check items that could block PO/signature.
- CS readiness: who will own onboarding milestones and when can we start kickoff post-signature?

If convenient, could you reply with a short update on the bullets above, or we can do a 20-min call tomorrow. Our finance team prefers we mark 50% commit if legal/PO are still pending, and 90–100% only when a signed MOA is in hand.

I’m attaching our current MAP for reference.

Thanks —
Karthik

Date: Sun, 3 Oct 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commit gating & CS readiness sync - Horizon Health (HZN-4382)

Karthik —

Thanks for the note and for the MAP. Quick answers: 

- Signed date: Internal procurement is optimistic about EOD Oct 22 but they'd like the final MOA in place by Oct 20 to route signatures.
- ARR uplift: We’re looking at a net-new spend of $420k ARR (annual invoicing). There’s one internal budget hold that could delay PO by ~1 week.
- Security: The SOC 2 attestation you provided looks good; we requested a brief note on data retention from your compliance team — Pat at procurement flagged that as last outstanding item.
- CS readiness: Monica — Luis will be our onboarding lead (cc’d). Once MOA is signed we expect kickoff materials to land within 5 business days and a phased launch across two product teams.

I’ll attach the version of the MOA with the procurement redlines. Can someone from your side confirm acceptance of section 3.4 (retention) or suggest a short addendum?

Appreciate the quick turnaround —
Sophie
Head of Partnerships | Horizon Health
sophie.barnes@horizonhealth.com

[Attachment: Horizon_MOA_v3.pdf (pdf)]

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commit gating & CS readiness sync - Horizon Health (HZN-4382)

Karthik / Priyom —

Quick internal note after Sophie's reply: 

- CS readiness: I can own the kickoff once MOA is signed. Proposed timeline:
  • Day 0–2: Contract closes and account handoff (we'll collect admin contacts).
  • Day 3–7: Technical onboarding and environment provisioning (we have a slot on Oct 25 if contract is done by Oct 20).
  • Week 2–6: Phased rollout and enablement.

- Risk flags: Procurement hang (~1 week) + the retention addendum. Priyom, can legal prep a 1-paragraph addendum accepting our standard 12-month retention with option to negotiate on enterprise plans? That should unblock procurement.

- Forecast guidance for finance: Given the signal (MOA in flight, procurement close likely Oct 22), recommend we book 60% commit for Q4 now, with the remaining 40% contingent on signed MOA. If procurement slips >2 weeks, move to 40% commit.

Let me know if you'd like me on the finance call tomorrow to present the CS timeline.

—Monica
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai

Sophie —

Appreciate the fast responses and the MOA. We’ll route a short retention addendum from Legal and aim to have it back to you by EOD Oct 6 (internal). Priyom — can you confirm?

For finance, we’ll mark HZN-4382 at 60% commit for Q4 today and note the contingency items: procurement PO and the retention addendum. If Horizon confirms PO by Oct 22 we’ll move to 90%+ commit.

Next steps: 
- Priyom to share 1-paragraph retention addendum by EOD Oct 6 (cc Sophie).
- Sophie to confirm final signer and expected PO date once procurement completes.
- Monica to pencil Sep 25–29 window for provisioning (assuming contract Oct 20).

Thanks everyone — I’ll update the HubSpot deal and finance thread once the addendum is shared.

Best,
